findings.finding: In-the-money stock options are left out of the per-share denominator. The engine divides by the 2,469,261,188 cover shares and says 'No incremental shares added today' (convertibles/warrants status 'missing'). The 2026-10-28 release reports Q3 diluted weighted shares of 2,582.9M against 2,467.2M basic: about 115.7M treasury-method option shares, roughly 4.7%. The 10-Q has option tables showing options outstanding at 2026-09-30. As a result, the fair value (136), the margin-of-safety entry price (86.9), every company_path EPS and every yearly table price are about 4.5% too high. The EPS path also uses basic shares (weighted_shares 2,469,261,188), so it is not the diluted EPS the multiples are meant to apply to.
findings.where: casefile val.case assumptions id 'dilution' / 'claims'; fc.anchors.opening.shares; company_path.fiscal_years.*.weighted_shares; inputs.json shares / dilutive instruments; source reading/release_2026-10-28__aph-ex99d1.txt line ~621 (Diluted 2,582.9) and reading/10q_2026-10-30.txt line ~5514 (options outstanding at 2026-09-30)
findings.fix: Enter the in-the-money options from the Q3 10-Q option table, using the treasury method or the release's diluted-minus-basic of about 115.7M as a cross-check, as dilutive instruments in inputs.json. Rerun ticker-value so that both the value per share and the EPS path use diluted shares.

findings.finding: The interest on existing debt is about half the reported run rate. fc.anchors.interest_rate_existing is 2.06% on 17.87B opening debt, about 0.37B a year. The Q3 2026 10-Q reports interest expense of 212.3M for Q3 and 633.9M for nine months (Q1 207.9M), about 0.85B a year or 4.7% on the debt. The new 4.625% and 5.300% notes plus the CommScope term loans explain the difference. The 2.06% is a pre-CommScope historical ratio. Pre-tax interest is therefore understated by about 0.48B a year, which overstates net income by about 0.37B and EPS by about 0.15 (about 4% of base FY2027 EPS 3.66) in all three scenarios. This feeds straight into the yearly bear/base/bull table through company_path EPS x multiple. Together with the dilution finding, the yearly table prices are about 8-9% too high.
findings.where: casefile fc.anchors.interest_rate_existing (0.02058); company_path.fiscal_years.*.net_income; source reading/10q_2026-10-30.txt line ~9494 (interest expense Q3 212.3, 9M 633.9)
findings.fix: Set the existing-debt interest rate from the 2026 run rate (Q3 212.3M x 4 / 17.87B = about 4.75%, or 9M 633.9M annualised / average debt) with evidence from the Q3 10-Q (web:pf_10q_20261030). Then rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: The base case pays above the company's own multiple history, yet it is labelled justified and carries no flag. Base company_path forward P/E runs 39.1 / 35.2 / 32.9 / 31.1 / 29.9 / 28.7 for years 0-5. The company's own forward P/E range for 2021-2025 is 20.8 / 25.1 / 28.6, so every base year sits above its own high. The only flag (peak_above_own_median) is on bull. The multiple is computed from ROIC 0.25, and that ROIC is evidenced: TTM NOPAT on capital was 23% at period end and 29% on average. What lifts the multiple is the EPS path, which rests on the engine-default growth fade (growth_half_life CONST, 3.0 years). That fade keeps base revenue growth above 10% a year through 2032 and at 15% real a year for 10 years, a path the engine itself says only 3% of companies this size achieved (warning growth_above_base_rate). In the base case, 2028 onward growth (19.6%, 16%, 14%, 12%, 11%) has no company evidence beyond the FY2027 override.
findings.where: casefile company_path.scenarios.base (justification justified_high, multiple_path) and company_path.flags; fc.driver_gaps growth_half_life; fc.warnings growth_above_base_rate; position/path.json company_path.scenarios.base
findings.fix: Show next to the result that the base forward P/E (39 falling to 29) is above APH's own 2021-2025 forward range (high 28.6), and that the base value depends on the engine-default growth fade, which has no company evidence after FY2027. The analyst_path part should either flag base as above own history or supply company evidence (orders, backlog, AI content per rack) for the FY2028+ growth half-life.

findings.finding: The bull ROIC of 0.32 is above its own cited evidence. The best number the evidence gives is the Q3 2026 peak quarter annualised: 3.02B x 4 x 0.75 / about 29.8B of capital = 30.4%, or 28.3% at the 27% adjusted tax rate (position/path.json gaps). The economics multiple then holds that 32% for 16 explicit years. This produces a year-0 multiple of 71.2 and a year-1 bull price of 312 (+292% in one year), against an own-history high of 28.6. The scenario is labelled 'peak' and carries a high flag, so it is visible, but the number itself is not backed by its source.
findings.where: casefile company_path.scenarios.bull.roic (0.32), economics.multiple_path; position/path.json company_path.scenarios.bull (evidence pf_operating_income_q_2026_09_30, nm_total_equity_q_2026_09_30, dc_fact_total_debt_20260930, nm_cash_q_2026_09_30)
findings.fix: Cap the bull ROIC at the evidenced peak, about 0.30 (Q3 annualised at a 25% tax rate), or cite evidence for 32%. Keep the peak flag. State next to the table that the bull yearly prices rest on one peak quarter held for 16 years.

findings.finding: 1.2B of committed acquisitions are not in opening debt. AdvancedPCB, Dexgreen and Humanetics Sensors are under definitive agreements, with two expected to close in Q4 2026 and one in Q1 2027, financed with cash and debt (10-Q). The guidance excludes them and so does the model. That is roughly neutral if their revenue is also left out, but the cash outflow (about 0.49 per share) is not shown.
findings.where: casefile fc.anchors.opening (debt 17.87B, cash 4.17B); source reading/10q_2026-10-30.txt line ~10723
findings.fix: Note the pending 1.2B of acquisitions as a known future cash outflow, or, if the repair pass touches inputs, add it as a committed draw with the acquired revenue.
